project: SF rental increase analysis (94122, building built 1940)
note: Every row was read from the official host during this session unless status says otherwise. 'verified' = page text read directly and quoted. 'reference' = official host linked but not line-read exhaustively. Unverified items are blank on the site and listed on flagged.html.

sources.title: Learn about rent increases in San Francisco — SF.gov (Rent Board)
sources.publisher: City and County of San Francisco — Rent Board
sources.used_for: 1.6% AGA 3/1/26-2/28/27 (60% of Bay Area CPI-U); 1.4% for 2025-26; base-rent-only calculation; no rounding up; anniversary-date rules; 30/90-day notice; +5 days if mailed; additional-occupants rule (no surcharge for new roommate); vacancy = no limit on initial rent; rent increase license requirement; notice must include dollar & percent increase, effective date

sources.title: Annual Rent Increase for 3/1/26 – 2/28/27 Announced — SF.gov News (Jan 14, 2026)
sources.publisher: City and County of San Francisco — Rent Board
sources.used_for: Official announcement: 1.6% annual allowable increase effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027; prior period 1.4%; worked $2,000 → $2,032 example

sources.title: 571 Allowable Annual Increases 26-27 (official Rent Board PDF, full history 1982-2027)
sources.publisher: City and County of San Francisco — Rent Board (media.api.sf.gov/documents/571_Allowable_Annual_Increases_26-27_1.pdf)

sources.title: Banked rent increases — SF.gov (Rent Board)
sources.publisher: City and County of San Francisco — Rent Board
sources.used_for: Banking rules: once every 12 months; a skipped increase is banked only after at least 24 full months pass without any increase, otherwise lost; no limit on total banked; not compounded or prorated (add percentages); banked amounts do not expire during a tenancy; do not carry to a new tenant; new owners may use prior owner's banked increases; rent increase license required; notice must state which part is banked

sources.title: Learn about San Francisco rental laws (coverage) — SF.gov (Rent Board)
sources.publisher: City and County of San Francisco — Rent Board
sources.used_for: Units built on or before June 13, 1979 may have rent control + eviction protection; units built before June 14, 1979 that are not single-family may have both; single-family/condo partial exemptions (Costa-Hawkins); subsidized-unit and hotel/hospital/dormitory exclusions; Rent Board counselor 415-252-4600 (weekdays 9-12 and 1-4); just-cause eviction grounds

sources.title: The Rent Board Housing Inventory (rent increase license) — SF.gov
sources.publisher: City and County of San Francisco — Rent Board
sources.used_for: All residential property owners must report into the Housing Inventory by March 1 annually; tenant-occupied units generate a rent increase license; a landlord MUST have a current rent increase license on the effective date of any annual or banked increase or the increase is not enforceable; requirement operative July 1, 2022 (condominiums and buildings with fewer than 10 units: March 1, 2023); reporting free; portal https://portal.sfrb.org/

sources.title: Limits on Rent Increases (statewide + local chart) — CA Office of the Attorney General
sources.publisher: State of California — Department of Justice, Office of the Attorney General
sources.used_for: Statewide TPA cap chart: San Francisco Area (Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, San Francisco, San Mateo counties) 6.3% for increases starting 8/1/25-7/31/26 and 8.8% for 8/1/26-7/31/27; local chart San Francisco row: units with CO before 6/13/79, one increase of up to 60% of CPI, banking allowed, 1.6% for 3/1/26-2/28/27; local rule applies when lower than statewide; new-tenant initial rent may be set freely (both state and local); page is informational, Civil Code §1947.12 governs

sources.title: Civil Code § 1947.12 (Tenant Protection Act of 2019 rent cap) — California Legislative Information
sources.publisher: State of California — Legislative Information (leginfo)
sources.used_for: Annual cap = 5% + cost-of-living change or 10%, whichever lower, of lowest gross rent charged in prior 12 months; max two increments per 12-month period; new tenancy initial rate uncapped; (d)(3) exemption: housing subject to stricter local rent control is excluded from the state cap; 15-year rolling construction exemption; single-family/condo exemption only if alienable separate + owner not REIT/corporation/LLC (natural person) with notice

sources.title: Civil Code § 827 (notice of rent increase) — California Legislative Information
sources.publisher: State of California — Legislative Information (leginfo)
sources.used_for: ≤10% increase (alone or combined in 12 months): ≥30 days' written notice; >10%: ≥90 days' written notice; delivery personally or by mail per CCP §1013 (adds 5 days); notice operates to amend the lease if tenant holds over

sources.title: Civil Code § 1942.5 (retaliation prohibited) — California Legislative Information
sources.publisher: State of California — Legislative Information (leginfo)
sources.used_for: No rent increase within 180 days after tenant's good-faith complaint re: habitability / exercise of rights; waiver void as against public policy; anti-retaliation applies to rent actions

sources.title: Housing Discrimination Under the Fair Housing Act — HUD
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development
sources.used_for: FHA prohibits housing discrimination because of race, color, national origin, religion, sex, familial status, disability; applies to nearly all housing; enforcement via HUD FHEO (complaints: https://www.hud.gov/reporthousingdiscrimination); Region IX (San Francisco) office: (415) 489-6524 / (800) 347-3739

sources.title: Housing (FEHA) — California Civil Rights Department
sources.publisher: State of California — Civil Rights Department
sources.used_for: FEHA prohibits discrimination/harassment in all aspects of renting; protected characteristics include race, religion, national origin, immigration status, primary language, source of income, familial status, disability, marital status, age, military status; retaliation for exercising rights prohibited; CRD enforces

sources.title: DOJ Sues RealPage for Algorithmic Pricing Scheme (Aug 23, 2024) — U.S. Department of Justice (archived)
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Public Affairs (Press Release 24-1047)
sources.used_for: How corporate landlords price: algorithmic revenue-management software alleged to coordinate rents via nonpublic competitor data; DOJ + 8 states alleged Sherman Act §§1-2 violations; ~80% market share allegation; complaint sought to end the practice

sources.title: DOJ Requires RealPage to End Sharing of Competitively Sensitive Information (Nov 24, 2025) — U.S. Department of Justice
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Public Affairs (Press Release 25-1111)
sources.used_for: Proposed consent judgment (Nov 24, 2025): RealPage must stop using competitors' nonpublic data at runtime; model training limited to historic/backward-looking data aged 12+ months; no sub-state-level geographic model effects; court-appointed monitor; Tunney Act comment process; court may enter final judgment

sources.title: Civil Code § 51 (Unruh Civil Rights Act) — California Legislative Information
sources.publisher: State of California — Legislative Information
sources.used_for: Reference link for state anti-discrimination coverage of business establishments (housing). Not quoted on the site; linked for manual review alongside S11/S12.

sources.title: Absence of a federal residential rent cap (analysis, not a source quote)
sources.publisher: Analysis based on reviewed federal housing statutes/pages (HUD, DOJ, leginfo)
sources.used_for: No federal statute caps residential rent increases nationwide; federal role is anti-discrimination enforcement (FHA) and antitrust (RealPage). Labeled ANALYSIS; nothing on the site asserts a federal rent cap exists.
